full_judgment:
Anwarul Hoque Choudhury, J. : This application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is directed against Memo No. SPRM/Forest/27/92-93/135 dated 15.9.92 issued by the Additional Chief Manager of Sylhet Pulp and Paper Mills Limited, Chatak, Sunamgonj giving the provisional work order in favour of respondent No. 6 Mr. MA Momit (Asuk) Annexure 'N'. 

 2. It is the case of the petitioner that he is doing his business with Sylhet Pulp and and Paper Mills. Limited for quite some time. The said Mills published a tender notice for supplying Mariti (bamboo) from the Juri Range within Putichura, Halampachora, Begunchori and Kulaura range, the said tender notice was issued under the signature of the General Manager of the said Mills (Respondent No. 4). 

 3. The petitioner on the basis of the terms and condition of the said tender notice participated in the above tender and he deposited Taka 1,00,000.00 as earnest money and the authority accepted the same. The petitioner wrote a letter to the Managing Director of the said Mills for making some correction in the demand draft. The said having been accepted the petitioner deposited the earnest money. The respondent No. 6 also participated in the above tender although he has no valid document to quality for the same. On 12.12.91 a letter was issued by the General-Manager for opening tender on 17.12.91. On 18.2.92 a letter of indent was issued by the respondent No. 5 namely Deputy Manager of the said Mills stating the fact that he accepted the tender filed by respondent No. 6 namely MA Momit (Asuk); Managing Director M Co. Trading International Limited. The petitioner being a lowest bidder went to the office of the said mills for ascertaining the fact and requested the authority to issue letter of indent in his favour but to no result. Thereafter on 23.6.92 he filed an application for demanding justice and cancellation of application for acceptance of tender in favour of respondent No. 6 (Annexure D) but also to no result. Thereafter according to the petitioner two board meetings of the said Mills were held on 25.6.92 and on 2.8.92 where it was decided that to put an end to the controversy a retender be called. The petitioner filed an application before the Chairman, Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation on 4.7.92 stating all facts and the Financial Director ordered for an inquiry report (Annexure 'A' and 'F). The inquiry report was considered by the Board of the said Mills and again the Mills decided that there should be a re-tender. The petitioner filed an application before the Hon'ble Minister, Ministry of Industry, Government of Bangladesh (Annexure 'G') stating all facts but to no result. When that was the matter a letter of provisional work order was issued in favour of respondent No. 6 without considering the case of the petitioner which is in violation of the principle of natural justice. The petitioner thereafter served demand of justice notice but till today no reply was made. 

 11. From the report of the Enquiry Committee, an one man Enquiry Committee of the Mill (Annexure 'K' page 18) it appears that the Enquiry Committee, in its report, written in Bengali and translated into English, reports to the effect inter alia which is a very exhaustive report made after hearing all including the petitioner that for collecting and cutting bamboo from the Bamboo Mahal which belonged to the government tender was floated on 25.9.91 on two envelope system and five tenders were submitted. It was amongst the 5 tenderers, M/s Sharif & Co. (the petitioner submitted the tender but his tender did not contain the full earnest money as per tender condition No. 7. Taka 55,000.00 was the earnest money money but only Tk. 45,000.00 (being the demand draft issued from the Pubali Bank, Darga Gate, Sylhet) was submitted. The earnest money submitted by Ws Sharif & Co. falling, short of Tk. 10,000.00 the tender committee declared the tender of M/s Sharif & Co. to be unacceptable and it was rejected and No. 2 envelope was returned to Sharif & Co. They refused to accept it. The shortage of earnest money is not disputed by Sharif & Co. because the demand draft is given by Bank for Tk. 45,000.00 and not for Tk. 55,000.00 as in the tender schedule but Sharif & Co. namely the petitioner argued before the Tender Committee that it is the fault of the Bank and not their fault. The- Bank was in a hurry to issue the demand draft for Tk. 45,000.00 when it would be Tk. 55;000.00 and in fact they have deposited with the Bank the entire money for the demand draft of Tk. 55,000.00; The enquiry officer found that it was the contention of Sharif & Co. before him that on the very day of the opening the tender 29.5.91 the Bank Manager, who issued the demand draft came to the Mills gate at 4.50 in the evening with the rest Tk. 10,000.00 demand draft in favour of the mill but he found no senior officer in the Mills. He therefore, rang up the Additional Accountant at his residence but the officer advised him to submit the demand draft officially and not at his home. On that advice oh 26.9.91 the Managing Director of M/s. Sharif & Co. gave Tk. 10,000.00 demand draft to the Mill Manager and requested him to accept the tender and it was accepted with "Note" of the Managing Director 'of the Mills. But during enquiry no such note was made available to the Enquiry Officer and no Officer of the Mill had been able to show the acceptance of the earnest money on 26.9.91 by the 'Note' as claimed by Sharif & Co. On 17.2.92 the other tender envelopes were opened and a list was prepared of the valid tenders in which list the name of Sharif & Co was not included and it is noted by the tender committee vide note dated 18.2.92 that the tender of Sharif & Co. has not been accepted because of the shortfall of Tk. 10,000.00 of earnest money and the tender committee recommended that the tender be given in favour of the next. The enquiry committee further found that person who submitted a tender had a duty to see that his tender is in perfect form and with the papers as required. He cannot shift his liability and responsibility by blaming the Bank Manager and the Committee also examined the Bank papers which issued the demand draft and found some discrepancy in those also and the Committee came to a finding that the claim that on that day another demand draft was issued may not be all true.
